claims.text: Increasing surface-defect density in transition-metal catalysts enhances ORR activity.
Surface defects enhance ORR activity by creating additional active sites.
Surface defects locally modulate catalyst electronic structure.
The defect-related activity enhancement is independent of overall catalyst composition and morphology.
The initial catalysts have uniform composition and morphology and a low baseline surface-defect density.
Controlled thermal annealing or plasma treatment can systematically increase surface-defect density while leaving overall composition unchanged.
Controlled thermal annealing or plasma treatment can increase surface-defect density while maintaining the catalyst's electronic structure.
The comparison will evaluate ORR in a standardized electrochemical cell, such as 0.1 M HClO4, with controlled temperature and oxygen concentration.
Vacancies and step edges serve as additional catalytic active sites.
Vacancies and step edges locally perturb catalyst electronic structure.
Defect-induced localized electronic perturbations lower the activation barrier for oxygen adsorption.
Defect-induced localized electronic perturbations lower the activation barrier for subsequent oxygen reduction.
Lower oxygen adsorption and reduction barriers increase catalytic turnover.
High-defect catalysts will exhibit higher specific ORR activity than low-defect controls.
High-defect catalysts will exhibit higher mass ORR activity than low-defect controls.
The mechanism is expected to apply in acidic fuel-cell environments at ambient to moderately elevated temperatures and typical ORR pressures.
The quantitative activity effect may vary because other surface properties and defect types can also influence ORR activity.
Surface strain and ligand effects can both influence the catalytic activity of PtCo core-shell-like nanowires.
TEM, XPS, or related microscopy and spectroscopy can be used to characterize surface-defect density.
The hypothesis is falsified if the high-defect catalyst shows no statistically significant ORR activity increase, or shows a decrease, relative to the otherwise identical low-defect control.

contradictions.description: The intervention is said to maintain constant electronic structure, whereas the hypothesis, mediator, and mechanism require defects to perturb or modulate the local electronic structure.
